title: Traceflow sampler field report: microburst and long-tail breakdown
content:
Summary:
This is a field-style report from a 3-week investigative run of the new traceflow sampler (v0.6). Goal: surface per-stage latency contributors across steady-state and microburst regimes, with explicit p50/p95/p99 reporting and lightweight repro instructions so SRE/infra can reproduce hot cases. This write-up mixes sampled trace examples, cohort summaries, and prioritized hypotheses.

Why this runs:
- Recent customer incidents showed transient p99 spikes that didn’t correlate with GPU utilization or queue depth traces.
- Existing sampling skewed toward short, single-token responses and missed the 2–5% of requests that account for tail cost.
- We want a reproducible sampler that balances coverage (seqlen, route, model-variant, warm/cold cache) and cost.

What we changed in the sampler:
- Adaptive stratified sampling by sequence-length band (0-32, 33-128, 129-512, 513+) and route type (chat, generate, embed).
- Event-aligned snapshots: record stage timestamps for tokenization, authorization, KV cache lookup, batch-wait, attention-emit, output-serialize, egress.
- Microburst detector: flag traces where CPU or GPU queue depth rose >3x baseline for >50ms during the request life.
- Low-overhead trace payloads (max 2KB) to avoid perturbing observed latencies.

Dataset & workload:
- Production-mimic replay of 48 hours of anonymized request headers and sequence length distributions from hosted-api (week-of-2024-11-04).
- Two model families exercised: rdx-70B-fp16 (prod) and rdx-7B-q4 (fallback).
- Mix: 82% chat, 12% generation (longform), 6% embeddings.

Key aggregated numbers (end-to-end response time, categorical p50/p95/p99):
- All requests (N=1.2M sampled): p50=38ms, p95=198ms, p99=820ms.
- Chat (N=984k): p50=34ms, p95=176ms, p99=760ms.
- Longform generate (N=144k): p50=110ms, p95=540ms, p99=2,300ms.
- Embeddings (N=72k): p50=18ms, p95=44ms, p99=180ms.

Per-stage median and tail notes (representative cohorts):
- Tokenization: p50=1.4ms, p95=3.2ms, p99=9.7ms (stable across cohorts).
- Auth & Quota check: p50=0.7ms, p95=2.6ms, p99=24ms (outliers where downstream auth cache missed).
- KV cache lookup: p50=0.5ms, p95=9ms, p99=120ms. 
  - Observed two modes: <2ms (cache hit) and 30–120ms (cache miss + remote index lookup).
- Batch wait (time spent in batching queue): p50=20ms, p95=120ms, p99=680ms.
  - Batch wait dominates longform tails. Microbursts push p99 up via queue amplification.
- Attention/compute phase: p50=6ms, p95=48ms, p99=250ms for 7B; p50=120ms, p95=640ms, p99=2,100ms for 70B.
- KV cache eviction/rehydration: when present adds median +18ms, tail +220ms.
- Serialization & egress: p50=1.8ms, p95=8.2ms, p99=42ms (protocol overhead and chunked streaming edge cases).

Notable trace archetypes found (examples):
1) Short chat p99 due to auth spike:
   - Sequence: tokenization (1.1ms) -> auth miss & remote (23ms) -> quick kv-hit (0.7ms) -> compute (5.8ms) -> egress (2.0ms); total 38.6ms but tail due to auth external call.
2) Longform microburst cascade:
   - Trigger: sudden influx of 8 concurrent longform requests routed to same GPU. Batch wait inflates to 540ms, attention stage 900ms (queuing on kernel), kv-cache misses for two requests add 110ms each, total ~1.8s.
3) Intermittent kernel contention in 70B pool:
   - Multiple traces show attention compute p95 close to p99 (640ms vs 2,100ms) when small background jobs (benchmarks) hit same GPU host - likely noisy-neighbor artifact.

Hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: Batch-queue amplification is the primary driver of p99 for longform workloads — mitigatable via adaptive max-batch-latency and burst isolation.
- H2: KV cache miss latency interacts nonlinearly with batch waits: cache misses free compute earlier but increase serialization overhead and can block batch scheduling.
- H3: Control-plane auth cache misses create disproportionate spikes for short requests; local auth caching TTL tuning could reduce auth p99.
- H4: Occasional co-located processes cause kernel contention on larger model hosts; need stricter host isolation or scheduling windows.

Quick repro steps for SRE/infra:
1) Replay the attached seed workload (confluence link) to the prod-like pool for 30 minutes at 1.2x normal QPS.
2) Enable traceflow sampler v0.6 (flags: sample-strata=seqlen, microburst=true, payload-max=2k).
3) On cluster with 70B GPUs, start a low-frequency background bench (local perf-runner -c 8) and observe p95/p99 divergence.
4) Toggle auth TTL from 30s->300s on a canary route and compare auth-stage p99 before/after.

Suggested mitigations & experiments (short-term to mid-term):
- Short-term (1–2 sprints): increase per-route auth caching TTLs, expose kv-cache miss metrics to router, add circuit-breaker to prevent large longform batches from forming in a single kernel queue.
- Mid-term (2–6 sprints): implement adaptive max-batch-latency that tightens for heavy longform traffic and relaxes for low-latency short-chat, introduce an eviction prefetcher to reduce kv miss tail, and add host-level scheduling to avoid running bench jobs on 70B hosts.
- Long-term: scheduler-aware model packing to ensure single-tenant or strict tenant isolation for highest-model classes; explore partial sequence offload to reduce per-token kernel load.

Open questions & follow-ups:
- What percentage of p99 longform incidents are reproducible vs one-offs? (Goal: measure reproducibility rate over 2 weeks).
- How much does adaptive batching hurt overall throughput and cost? Need A/B on canary pool.
- Can we instrument KV index service to return a coarse miss cost estimate to the router so it can de-prioritize or route away?

Appendix: Sampled trace JSON excerpts (anonymized) and short script to run local replay are in linked Confluence doc. Also attached: spreadsheets with cohort slices (by seqlen, model, route) and a short rundown of the sampler config knobs.

Owner notes (action items):
- Aisha: schedule infra repro window with SRE next week (blocked by infra change freeze on 2024-12-24).
- Marco: add kv-miss histogram to router telemetry and open quick PR.
- Chen: coordinate canary for auth TTL change and collect pre/post traces.
- Priya: design adaptive-batcher experiment and draft rollout plan (include rollback criteria).

Status: in_review — please add comments inline in the Confluence page linked above or ping the owner in #serving-runtime.

End of report.
